    StartersFive-note crackersSeeded crackers topped five ways: cream cheese, pâté, cheddar, salmon, figHow to make it20 seeded crackers80g cream cheese80g chicken liver pate80g cheddar, sliced100g smoked salmon1 sprig dill4 figs, halvedLay the crackers out in rows of five.Top each row with a different note: cream cheese, pate, cheddar, smoked salmon with dill, and fig.Serve straight away.Muncie sweetcorn frittersIndiana sweetcorn fritters with sour cream and chives, from Roy's home townHow to make it3 corn cobs150g self-raising flour2 eggs125ml milk3 spring onions, sliced1 tsp smoked paprika80ml vegetable oil150g sour cream1 chivesCut the kernels off the corn cobs.Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, paprika and a good pinch of salt into a thick batter, then stir in the corn and spring onions.Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and drop in heaped tablespoons of batter, pressing them flat.Fry 2 to 3 minutes a side until golden and cooked through, in batches, and drain on paper towel.Serve hot with sour cream and snipped chives.Tater tots with ketchupStack them up. This means something.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsMashed potato mountainButtery mash sculpted tall, with slow cooked onion gravy poured overHow to make it1.5kg floury potatoes200ml full cream milk120g butter2 brown onions, sliced1 tbsp plain flour400ml beef stockPeel and boil the potatoes until soft.Cook the onions slowly in some of the butter until golden.Stir in the flour, add the stock and simmer for gravy.Rice the potatoes and beat with the hot milk and the rest of the butter.Pile into a tall mountain and pour the gravy over.Neary family roast chickenThe family dinner that goes off the railsHow to make itAs written, serves 4Dry-brined chicken with thyme butter under the skin, roasted golden and crisp, with buttered peas and carrots and a simple pan gravy.Salt a 1.8kg chicken all over and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight.Mash 50g soft butter with thyme leaves and push it under the breast skin.Roast at 220°C for 20 minutes, then 180°C for 50 minutes until the juices run clear.Rest 15 minutes.Stir 1 tbsp flour into the pan juices, add 300ml chicken stock and simmer until thick.Boil 4 sliced carrots for 6 minutes and 300g frozen peas for 3, then toss in butter.SweetsDevils Tower cakeTall chocolate cake with ridged chocolate buttercreamHow to make it400g butter, soft250g caster sugar4 eggs250g self-raising flour90g cocoa200ml full cream milk350g icing sugarHeat the oven to 170°C and prepare three small tins. Beat half the butter with the sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs.Fold in the flour, some of the cocoa and the milk, divide between the tins and bake.Cool completely.Beat the remaining butter with the icing sugar and remaining cocoa for buttercream.Stack the layers tall, cover in buttercream and drag ridges with a fork.UFO meringuesSaucer shaped meringues with a dot of lemon curd underneathHow to make it3 egg whites180g caster sugar3 tbsp lemon curdWhisk the egg whites and sugar over simmering water until hot, then beat to stiff peaks.Pipe into flat saucer shapes with a small dome in the middle.Bake at 100°C, then cool in the oven.Spread a dot of lemon curd underneath.DrinksNeary kitchen strawberry lemonadeFresh strawberry and lemon juice lemonade over ice, no alcoholHow to make it300g strawberries120ml sugar syrup5 lemons700ml cold water1 bunch mint1 bag iceHull the strawberries, keeping a few to slice. Blitz most of them with the sugar syrup and strain into a jug.Stir in the lemon juice and the water.Add plenty of ice, sliced strawberries and lemon wheels.Pour into glasses and top with mint.Fresh orange juice in a carafeThe fridge got raided.
